sources.title: Tópicos para construção da ocupação pré-histórica do Cerrado
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis of Central Brazilian Cerrado archaeology, local hunter-gatherer sequences, pottery, horticulture and distinct settlement settings.

sources.title: Arqueologia e história indígena no Pantanal
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional synthesis of archaeological traditions, settlement evidence and Indigenous history in the Brazilian Pantanal.

sources.title: The Ring Villages of Central Brazil: A Challenge for Amazonian Archaeology
sources.note: Archaeological evidence for large ceramic agricultural ring villages beginning around 800 CE and changing regional sociopolitical organization.

sources.title: Etnoarqueologia de dois aterros Guató no Pantanal
sources.note: Indigenous archaeology and later Guató knowledge concerning persistent mounds, waterways, fishing places and constructed wetland landscapes.

sources.title: Ethnography of the Chaco, Handbook of South American Indians
sources.note: Smithsonian historical synthesis of distinct Chaco peoples, languages, subsistence, material culture and social organization, used cautiously as comparison.

sources.title: Warfare, Reorganization, and Readaptation at the Margins of Spanish Rule: The Chaco and Paraguay, 1573 to 1882
sources.note: Cambridge history of diverse Chaco and Paraná peoples, colonial warfare, labor demands, missions, mobility and Indigenous readaptation.

sources.title: South American Indians: Comparative material on habitation patterns and technology
sources.note: Smithsonian comparative synthesis of South American dwellings and settlement patterns, explicitly treated as broad and dated reference material.

sources.title: Persistent Early to Middle Holocene tropical foraging in southwestern Amazonia
sources.note: Excavation, radiocarbon and burial evidence for long-lived foraging settlements on forest islands in the Llanos de Moxos.

sources.title: Direct archaeological evidence for Southwestern Amazonia as an early plant domestication and food production centre
sources.note: Macrobotanical, phytolith and starch-residue methods demonstrating plant processing and domestication near the atlas umbrella western edge.

sources.title: Prehistoric Pathoecology as Represented by Parasites of a Mummy from the Peruaçu Valley, Brazil
sources.note: Paleoparasitological analysis of a Central Brazilian mummy associated with Una ceramics, cultivated plants and intestinal parasite evidence.

sources.title: Human ecological and social determinants of dental caries among the Xavante Indigenous people in Central Brazil
sources.note: Modern longitudinal health research and bioarchaeological comparison showing oral-health effects of major dietary and economic transitions.

sources.title: Indigenous Burning as Conservation Practice in Central Brazil
sources.note: Collaborative research on ceremonial and collective hunting fires and savanna recovery among Xavante communities in Central Brazil.

sources.title: Community owned solutions for fire management in tropical ecosystems
sources.note: Comparative case studies connecting Indigenous burning, hunting festivals, courtship, initiation and intergenerational knowledge transmission.

sources.title: Piqui e buriti: importância alimentar para a população dos cerrados
sources.note: Embrapa publication documenting the food value and processing potential of two prominent native Cerrado fruits.

sources.title: Nutritional status and socioeconomic change among Toba and Wichí populations of the Argentinean Chaco
sources.note: Modern health study summarizing historically mobile Chaco subsistence and documenting later nutrition changes under socioeconomic pressure.

sources.title: The Global and the Local: Health in Latin American Indigenous Women
sources.note: Long-term research with Toba communities on diet, reproductive health, mobility, land restriction and uneven colonial and market transitions.

sources.title: Food Intake and the Significance of Feeding in Qom Children of Northern Argentina
sources.note: Community-based study of Qom children, family food practices and modern subsistence change, used only as labeled later comparison.

sources.title: Pathways to Agency: Indigenous Wichi Caregiver-Infant Interactions
sources.note: Recent observational study of Wichi infants, caregivers, multiparty learning and gendered work, used only as labeled comparison.

sources.title: Notes on current Mbyá-Guarani medicinal plant exchanges in southern Brazil
sources.note: Community research on medicinal plant exchange, diagnosis, spiritual healing and care during pregnancy among specific modern Guarani communities.

sources.title: Outro lado da fronteira agrícola: origem e declínio da agricultura autóctone no cerrado
sources.note: Historical and archaeological synthesis of Una, Aratu-Sapucaí and Uru farming, shelters, crops and colonial disruption in the Cerrado.

sources.title: Genomic history of coastal societies from eastern South America
sources.note: Open ancient-DNA study demonstrating regional population histories, sparse sampling and relationships among Brazilian archaeological contexts.

sources.title: Negros da terra: índios e bandeirantes nas origens de São Paulo
sources.note: Museu Nacional dos Povos Indígenas catalog and synopsis of archival scholarship on raids, forced labor and Indigenous destruction.

sources.title: As Guerras Justas e a escravidão indígena em Minas Gerais nos séculos XVIII e XIX
sources.note: Historical analysis of colonial dehumanization, punitive expeditions, so-called just wars, enslavement and demographic violence in inland Brazil.

sources.title: Semelhanças, diferenças e rede de relações no Holoceno inicial no Brasil Central
sources.note: Technological study of Serranópolis and Central Brazilian lithic evidence emphasizing networks, local differences and limits of archaeological traditions.

sources.title: Vegetação Brasileira, IBGE
sources.note: Brazilian statistical agency classification distinguishing Cerrado savanna, Pantanal savanna-steppe, southern grasslands and other vegetation formations.

proposedOverrides.summary: Atlas umbrella for distinct South American communities; never one people or language.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact atlas geometry and South America coverage queue override an initial rejected African routing assumption.
The id is a residual subsistence umbrella across Cerrado, Pantanal, Gran Chaco and adjacent southern lowlands, not one people, state, language or archaeological tradition.
The exact feature is absent in 2000 BCE, appears in 1500 BCE, contracts sharply at 800 CE, disappears from 1492 to 1500, fragments at 1650 and disappears after 1783.
Repeated coordinate hashes and tiny decimal changes are treated as basemap reuse and drawing edits, never migrations.
Named Indigenous labels at the 1492 gap and colonial labels after 1650 are atlas taxonomy seams, not synchronized replacement or effective territorial control.
Regional archaeological traditions are material classifications, never automatic ethnic aliases.
Later ethnography is labeled comparison and never projected unchanged into the target interval.
Contemporaneous written-language sample: none is securely attributable to this atlas record. No shared target language or self-authored script spans the umbrella.
